newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end down on heavy liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end down on heavy liquidation.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended down on Thursday due to heavy liquidation of selective stocks late in the session with overseas investors losing interest in the market, brokers said.
The index dipped 0.122 points or 0.25 percent to 48.285 points, on volume of 7.9 million shares worth $3.1 million. Of 41 B shares, 34 traded, with 11 down, 14 flat and nine up.
"Overseas investors are not patient enough in the bearish market sentiment so that they unwound their positions despite such low prices," one broker said.
"The index is likely to consolidate around 48 points, an important level for both long and short position holders," a second broker said.
Shanghai Huili Building Material was the biggest loser on expectations of unpromising results, falling $0.010 or 5.37 percent to $0.176, on volume of 27.500 shares.
Shanghai Automation Instrumentation followed in the most active trading amid heavy overseas liquidation, down $0.006 or 4.41 percent to $0.130, on volume of 1.5 million shares.

Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development was the second most actively traded on heavy selling despite domestic institutional support, because investors do not want to buy its right issue, brokers said.
It ended down $0.010 or 1.07 percent to $0.920, on volume of 775,000 shares. The company has set a price of 5.50 yuan for a three-for-10 rights issue for all shareholders.
Shanghai A shares closed down on a technical correction following sharp gains in the past few days, but market sentiment is still bullish, brokers said.

The index fell 3.083 points or 0.29 percent to 1061.526 points on volume of 1.1 billion shares worth 9.3 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue chip index dropped 11.281 points or 0.42 percent to 2680.368 points.
Fujian Yaohua Glass was the biggest loser on institutional unwinding, down 1.35 yuan or 10.64 percent to 11.33 yuan, on volume of 11.3 million shares.
